lessons.title: Circles and ellipses
lessons.goal: Draw round shapes from the shoulder, not the fingers.
steps: Fill a page with circles the size of a coin, then the size of your palm. Move your whole arm.
Ghost each circle first: circle the pencil above the paper 2–3 times, then touch down.
Draw ellipses inside boxes: the long axis always runs through the middle.
Circle your best three. Notice which size is easiest.

lessons.title: Boxes in space
lessons.goal: Draw a cube that looks solid from any angle.
steps: Open the 3D sandbox and turn a cube slowly. Watch how its three visible faces change.
Draw the cube from three different angles you set in the sandbox.
Draw the hidden back edges lightly: they keep the box honest.
Compare: do parallel edges in your drawing lean the same way as in the sandbox?

lessons.title: Cylinders, cones and spheres
lessons.goal: Turn circles and boxes into round solids.
steps: In the 3D sandbox, look at a cylinder from above and from the side. The top ellipse gets thinner as you go down to eye level.
Draw five cylinders: the further below your eye, the rounder their top ellipse.
Draw a cone and a sphere with the same light; add a simple shadow.
Build a mug or a bottle from these shapes.

lessons.title: Confident lines
lessons.goal: Draw straight lines in one stroke.
steps: Mark two dots. Ghost the movement three times, then draw the line in one go.
Fill a page: short lines, long lines, all directions.
Don't go over a line twice; draw a new one beside it instead.
Circle your straightest lines.

lessons.title: Line weight
lessons.goal: Use thin and thick lines to show depth.
steps: Open the line-weight chart in Guides and copy each line with your pencils.
Draw a box: thin lines on the lit side, thicker lines where it touches the table and in shadow.
Draw a near and a far object: thicker outlines for the near one.
Compare with a version using one weight only.

lessons.title: Contour drawing
lessons.goal: Follow edges slowly and accurately.
steps: In the Studio, convert a photo to Contours and look at the main edges.
Draw the object's outer contour slowly, eyes on the object more than the paper.
Add the inner contours: folds, overlaps, edges of shadows.
Overlay your drawing with the Compare screen to check.

lessons.title: Measuring with your pencil
lessons.goal: Compare sizes by eye and with a pencil held at arm's length.
steps: Hold the pencil at arm's length, close one eye, and measure the height of an object with the pencil tip and your thumb.
Compare: how many of those heights fit in its width?
Mark the height and width on paper first, then draw inside those marks.
Check with the grid in Guides or Prepare.

lessons.title: Face proportions
lessons.goal: Place eyes, nose and mouth with the classical canon.
steps: Open Face proportions in Guides over a portrait photo and move the box onto the face.
Check the rules: eyes halfway down, five eye-widths across, nose base and chin in thirds.
Draw the head oval and the guide lines lightly, then place the features.
Note where this face differs from the canon: that's what makes it this person.

lessons.title: Figure proportions
lessons.goal: Draw a standing figure about 8 heads tall.
steps: Open Figure proportions in Guides; mark 8 equal head units down the page.
Place the landmarks: nipples at 2, navel at 3, crotch at 4 (half), knees at 6.
Draw a simple stick figure on those marks, then add the masses: ribcage, pelvis, limbs.
Try 6 heads (a child) and compare.

lessons.title: One-point perspective
lessons.goal: Draw a road, a room or a corridor going into the distance.
steps: In Guides choose Perspective → 1-point on blank paper. Note the horizon at eye level and one vanishing point.
Draw boxes floating above, below and on the horizon; their depth lines all go to the point.
Draw a road or corridor with doors and windows.
Print the guide and draw over it, or save it as a reference.

lessons.title: Two-point perspective
lessons.goal: Draw buildings and objects seen from a corner.
steps: Choose 2-point perspective. Keep both points far apart, even outside the picture: close points distort.
Draw a box from its nearest vertical edge, then send its top and bottom edges to each point.
Make a small street of boxes; add roofs, doors and windows.
In the 3D sandbox, turn on vanishing points for a cube and compare.

lessons.title: Three-point perspective
lessons.goal: Draw tall things seen from below or above.
steps: Choose 3-point perspective; the third point sits far below (looking down) or above (looking up).
Draw a tall building whose verticals all lean to the third point.
In the 3D sandbox, look down at a tall box and turn on vanishing points.
Draw the same building from below and from above.

lessons.title: Light, form shadow and cast shadow
lessons.goal: Tell the shadow on an object from the shadow it throws.
steps: In the 3D sandbox, move the light around a sphere and a cube.
Name the parts: light side, form shadow (on the object), cast shadow (on the ground).
Draw the sphere with the three zones only.
Move the light lower: cast shadows get longer. Draw that too.

lessons.title: Three-value studies
lessons.goal: See a picture as light, middle and dark.
steps: In the Studio, convert a photo with Three values.
Draw small (about 8 cm) studies using only paper white, one mid grey and one dark.
Squint at the photo: details disappear, big value shapes remain.
Do three studies of different photos.

lessons.title: Reflected light and core shadow
lessons.goal: Make round forms look really round.
steps: Look at a white ball on a table near a window.
Find the core shadow: the darkest band of the form shadow, just past the turning point.
Find the reflected light: a slightly lighter edge inside the shadow, bounced from the table.
Draw the ball with these two details; keep the reflected light darker than any lit part.

lessons.title: Value scale
lessons.goal: Control pencil pressure from very light to very dark.
steps: Draw a strip of 9 boxes. Fill them from white to your darkest dark, evenly stepped.
Use the Studio's Colour → value conversion to see a picture as these 9 steps.
Repeat with a softer pencil (4B or 6B) and compare the darkest box.
Keep the best scale as a reference.

lessons.title: Hatching and crosshatching
lessons.goal: Shade with lines instead of smudges.
steps: Open Crosshatching in the Studio to see how darker areas get more line directions.
Shade a 9-step scale with hatching: tighter lines, then a second and third direction.
Shade a cube: one direction for the light side, two for the side, three for the cast shadow.
Shade a sphere with lines that follow its curve.

lessons.title: Smooth gradients
lessons.goal: Shade without visible strokes.
steps: Shade a long strip from dark to light with small overlapping circles, light pressure, many layers.
Build darks in layers instead of pressing hard.
Shade a cylinder: the gradient runs across, not along it.
Compare a blended and an unblended version: which reads better?

lessons.title: Soft, rough, shiny
lessons.goal: Suggest a surface with marks.
steps: Make four squares: wood, stone, metal, fabric. Fill each with marks that feel like it.
Shiny: high contrast, sharp highlights. Soft: low contrast, soft edges.
Draw the same apple as shiny plastic and as a peach.
Only add texture in the light-to-mid areas; shadows hide it.

lessons.title: Texture that follows form
lessons.goal: Bend patterns and marks around a round surface.
steps: Draw stripes on a flat paper strip, then on a cylinder: on the cylinder they curve like ellipses.
In the 3D sandbox, look at the sphere in wireframe: the lines show how marks wrap around it.
Draw an orange: the dimples get smaller and closer together near its edges.
Draw a striped sweater sleeve; the stripes follow the folds.

lessons.title: Hair and fur
lessons.goal: Draw hair as masses first, strands last.
steps: Simplify the hair into 3–5 big shapes with the Studio's Posterize or Three values.
Shade the masses: light, mid, dark.
Add strands only at the edges and in the light, following the flow.
Lift highlights with an eraser.

lessons.title: Rule of thirds
lessons.goal: Place the subject where the eye likes it.
steps: Open Composition → Thirds in Guides over a few of your photos.
Find where the main subject sits: centre, or on a third line?
Draw three thumbnails (small boxes) of the same scene with the subject in different places.
Pick the one you like best and say why.

lessons.title: Negative space
lessons.goal: Draw the spaces between things.
steps: In the Studio, convert a photo of a chair or plant with Negative space.
Draw only the empty shapes around the object, not the object.
The object appears by itself; check its proportions.
Do the same with a hand making a gesture.

lessons.title: Thumbnail planning
lessons.goal: Plan a drawing in small value sketches.
steps: Draw six 5 × 4 cm boxes.
Sketch the same scene in each, changing viewpoint, crop or light.
Use only three values in each.
Choose the strongest and enlarge it with the grid in Prepare.

lessons.title: Gesture drawing
lessons.goal: Capture the movement of a pose in seconds.
steps: Open Timed practice with 30-second mannequin poses.
For each pose draw one curved line of action first (head to the supporting foot).
Add the head, ribcage and hips as simple shapes; stop when time runs out.
Do two rounds; the second is always freer.

lessons.title: The mannequin
lessons.goal: Build a figure from simple 3D forms.
steps: Use 2-minute mannequin poses in Timed practice.
Draw the ribcage as an egg, the pelvis as a box, limbs as cylinders.
Show which limbs are nearer by overlapping them.
Keep the 8-head proportions from the proportions lessons.

lessons.title: Hands
lessons.goal: Draw hands from boxes and cylinders.
steps: Draw the palm as a flat box, fingers as three cylinders each.
Use your own hand in different poses as the reference (Timed practice → your pictures).
Check that each finger's joints line up in curved rows.
Try the hand holding a cup.

lessons.title: A finished portrait
lessons.goal: Combine proportions, values and edges.
steps: Start a project from a portrait photo with the Realistic style.
Follow the guided steps; use Face proportions in Guides to check the features.
Shade in three values first, then refine.
Compare with the original in the Compare screen and fix the biggest difference.

lessons.title: Still life with light
lessons.goal: Draw a group of objects with one light.
steps: Set up three objects by a window, or build them in the 3D sandbox.
Plan with thumbnails; mark the light direction on the page.
Draw shapes, then shadows (form and cast), then textures.
Record a timelapse with camera tracing to see your process.

lessons.title: A street in perspective
lessons.goal: A detailed scene with depth.
steps: Set up 2-point perspective in Guides with the horizon low.
Block in buildings as boxes, then cut in doors, windows and roofs.
Use line weight: thick near, thin far.
Add people at eye level: their heads all touch the horizon.
